$schema-note: Dated, justified, SCOPED allowlist for the OSV dependency gate (scripts/osv-gate.mjs, .github/workflows/osv-scan.yml) and the nightly re-scan of published packages (scripts/audit-shipped-npm.mjs). A finding is suppressed ONLY by an entry here, so the gate can never be silently neutered. It covers both kinds of finding the gate fails on: a malicious-package advisory (`MAL-…`; suppress only a confirmed false positive) and a NEW HIGH/CRITICAL or unscored vulnerability. Each entry suppresses ONE advisory on ONE package at ONE version in ONE lockfile, never an advisory id everywhere. Each entry MUST carry: `id` (the advisory id or any alias: MAL-…, GHSA-…, CVE-…, GO-…), `package` (exact name), `version` (exact version), `lockfile` (exact repo-relative path of the lockfile the finding appears in; for the nightly re-scan of the published npm packages that is `package-lock.json`, the lockfile of its scratch install), `justification` (at least 20 characters: why it is accepted, not exploitable in our usage, no fix available, upstream confirmed false positive), `added` (ISO date) and `expires` (ISO date, REQUIRED, at most 180 days after `added`). Past its expiry the entry stops suppressing and the risk must be re-justified. Wildcards, ranges and unknown keys are rejected. Bump the dependency FIRST; allowlist only when there is no fix. Mirrors security/npm-audit-allowlist.json.

allow.justification: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns. No patched release exists: 3.0.3 is the newest braces on npm and the advisory lists no fixed version, so there is nothing to bump to. The flaw is stack exhaustion on a pattern of deeply nested braces; in this workspace it sits under the dev tools @turbo/gen (node-plop -> globby -> fast-glob) and vinext (vite-plugin-commonjs -> vite-plugin-dynamic-import -> fast-glob), where braces only expands glob patterns taken from first-party source and config, never request-supplied or attacker-controlled input. Re-triage when braces publishes a fix.

uuid: Missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6 when buf is provided. uuid 8.3.2 (fixed in 11.1.1+): the missing bounds check needs a `buf` argument to v3/v5/v6. It is pulled in by @google-cloud/storage (directly and via gaxios and teeny-request), and every call site in the installed 7.19.0 closure is `uuid.v4()` with no buffer (resumable-upload, request id headers, multipart boundary), so the vulnerable path is not reachable. A workspace override to 11+ would make our tests exercise a combination consumers never get, because overrides do not ship with the published package. Same justification as the package-lock.json entry for the published closure; remove once @google-cloud/storage ships a gaxios on uuid >= 11.1.1.

source-map-js allows event-loop denial of service through indexed source-map section offsets. source-map-js 1.2.1 (fixed 1.2.2) is postcss's source-map reader. The event-loop DoS needs an attacker-supplied indexed source map; postcss here only reads maps of first-party CSS during the fixture's build. The fixture (standalone-drain-app) is a frozen lockfile installed into a throwaway build directory by a docker or build e2e, never shipped, never serving traffic, and its pin is the thing under test; the Docker-based suites that install it cannot run in this change, so it is not bumped blind. Fixtures are deliberately pinned and exempt from Dependabot (tests/dependabot-ecosystems.test.ts), so re-triage at expiry.
